title: Zealand Pharma, Generate strike AI obesity drug deal worth up to $1.2 billion
source_used: Yahoo Finance (carries Reuters text); Reuters page blocked (HTTP 401)
key_facts: Zealand Pharma and Generate Biomedicines said on Tuesday 13 Oct 2026 they have partnered to develop protein-based treatments for obesity and other metabolic diseases using AI, in a deal worth up to nearly $1.2 billion.
Generate will receive $30 million upfront and up to $35 million in early preclinical milestones.
It could earn nearly $1.2 billion in development, regulatory and commercial milestones, the companies said.
Generate will lead research through lead-candidate selection; Zealand will oversee clinical development, regulatory submissions and commercialisation.
Generate is based in Somerville, Massachusetts; its shares were up about 5 percent in extended trading.
Zealand's shares trade in Copenhagen (ticker ZEAL.CO on the page).
quote_evidence: Oct 13 (Reuters) - Zealand Pharma and Generate Biomedicines said on Tuesday they have partnered to develop protein-based treatments for obesity and other metabolic diseases using AI, in a deal worth up to nearly $1.2 billion.

Generate will receive $30 million upfront and up to $35 million in early preclinical milestones and could earn nearly $1.2 billion in development, regulatory and commercial milestones, the companies said.
Generate will lead research through lead-candidate selection, while Zealand will oversee clinical development, regulatory submissions and commercialization.
why_it_matters_hint: A drug maker pays for an AI protein-design platform for obesity drugs, but only the upfront payment is certain.
notes: Reuters original blocked (HTTP 401); the Reuters text, with its dateline and reporter credit, is carried by Yahoo Finance. GlobeNewswire press release and FirstWord were blocked or empty. Whether the milestone figure includes the upfront is not stated.
